properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): a claim's proof_status.total_steps adds up its lines of proof, so a step two lines share counts twice. One walk serves two questions, "is this line wholly confirmed?" and "how many steps are under this claim?", and nothing ever said what total_steps counts
properties.source: the root-cause skill, run by Claude in this session on @ajs's "/root-cause double-counting and a walk that never reaches refuted claims"; measured on reflow2 main 5a94e83 locally and on flo2.io 0.86.0
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-18.

① OBSERVED. On flo2.io 0.86.0, get_node on design bbcd344a71ff1cbd gives:
- req:prop-uniqueness (two concluding steps, inf:u-8-strong-induction and inf:u2-7-reductio): proof_status.total_steps 47;
- req:thm-fundamental-theorem-of-arithmetic (one step, whose premises include uniqueness): 41.
A claim reports more steps than the theorem built on it. Expected: the distinct steps under a claim, so the theorem ≥ uniqueness. NOT affected: claims with one concluding step, and loop_status's design-wide count (48, distinct).

② PRECEDENT: none. search_design in reflow2 and in flo2 found only today's flo2 #169 records (cap:the-proof-read-back-counts-refuted-claims-and-every-step-the-same-way), which found the number and pinned it without fixing it.

③ CANDIDATES:
- (a) IMPLEMENTATION: proof_reading sums per-line walks, each from a cloned visited set.
- (b) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: the design really holds duplicate step records.
- (c) OUTSIDE reflow2: flo2's gateway alters the number.
- (d) INTENT: total_steps was never defined. ProofReading's doc says only "proof status … with why", and cap:proof-who-confirmed says "walking the derivation chain" (singular), so the per-line walk was never wrong against a stated meaning.
- (e) ASSURANCE: no test covers a claim with two holding lines that share steps.

④⑤ MEASURED on the committed fixture crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/fixtures/proof_trial_rung_2_fta.json (128 nodes, 48 distinct Inferences), imported into a scratch store and read with a local main build (no gateway):
- uniqueness 47, theorem 41, existence 11, identical to flo2.io, so (c) is REFUTED;
- counting distinct Inference ids from the fixture's CONCLUDES and PREMISE_OF edges: line 1 has 27 steps and line 2 has 20, with 7 shared; 27 + 20 = 47 (the reported number) and the union is 40. So (b) is REFUTED (40 distinct, no duplicates), and (a) SURVIVES, with the sum reproduced exactly;
- the theorem's 41 equals its distinct count, because one line walks with one visited set;
- (d) is CONFIRMED by reading: no definition of total_steps exists in the code doc, the capability or the requirement;
- (e) is CONFIRMED: no test outside inference.rs asserts total_steps, and none builds two holding lines with a shared step.

⑥ CLASS. Two quantities, a per-line judgement and a per-claim set size, are computed by one walk. The total inherited the per-line semantics because the total's meaning was never written down. It already struck rung 1: on flo2.io, d2ea1acfee6090c8's theorem (two lines, Euclid and Goldbach, sharing a lemma) reports total_steps 26 in a design that holds 25 steps.

PROPOSED FIX (not built):
- total_steps, confirmed_steps and unconfirmed_steps count the UNION of the steps under every holding line, each step once;
- "proven" stays a per-line judgement;
- the count's meaning is written on ProofReading and in the served text;
- the pin is a CLASS invariant: for every concluded claim, total_steps equals the number of distinct Inferences reachable below it through holding lines, and never exceeds the design's Inference count. It is run on both trial fixtures.
- flo2's real-engine test that pins today's summed number (#169) is moved when reflow2 ships the fix.

COULD NOT ESTABLISH: whether any consumer besides flo2's read-back relies on the summed number. A search of reflow2's tests found none.
